sanskrit: sa tu rājan dhanuś chittvā pāṇḍavasya mahāmṛdhe athainaṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ viṃśatyā samavākirat
english: But he, O king, having cut apart the bow of the Pāṇḍava in that great battle, then covered him, now bowless, with twenty arrows.

sanskrit: tato 'nyad dhanur ādāya bhīmaseno mahārathaḥ avākirat tava sutaṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Then, taking up another bow, Bhīmasena the mighty chariot-warrior overwhelmed your son with shafts and cried, "Stand! Stand!"

sanskrit: mahad āsīt tayor yuddhaṃ citrarūpaṃ bhayānakam yādṛśaṃ samare pūrvaṃ jambhavāsavayor abhūt
english: Great was the combat between those two, wondrous in form and terrible, such as once raged in olden days between Jambha and Vāsava.

sanskrit: tayos tatra śarair muktair yamadaṇḍanibhaiḥ śubhaiḥ samācchannā dharā sarvā khaṃ ca sarvā diśas tathā
english: By the bright arrows loosed by those two, arrows like the rod of Yama, the whole earth was veiled, and the sky, and all the quarters likewise.

sanskrit: tataḥ śrutarvā saṃkruddho dhanur āyamya sāyakaiḥ bhīmasenaṃ raṇe rājan bāhvor urasi cārpayat
english: Then Śrutarvan, swollen with wrath, drawing his bow, struck Bhīmasena in battle, O king, upon the arms and the breast with his shafts.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho mahārāja tava putreṇa dhanvinā bhīmaḥ saṃcukṣubhe kruddhaḥ parvaṇīva mahodadhiḥ
english: Pierced deep, O great king, by your bow-wielding son, Bhīma, enraged, heaved like the great ocean at the turning of the moon.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo ruṣāviṣṭaḥ putrasya tava māriṣa sārathiṃ caturaś cāśvān bāṇair ninye yamakṣayam
english: Then Bhīma, seized by fury, O lord, sent your son's charioteer and his four horses with his arrows to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: virathaṃ taṃ samālakṣya viśikhair lomavāhibhiḥ avākirad ameyātmā darśayan pāṇilāghavam
english: Marking him robbed of his chariot, that hero of measureless spirit covered him with feathered shafts, displaying the swiftness of his hand.

sanskrit: śrutarvā viratho rājann ādade khaḍgacarmaṇī athāsyādadataḥ khaḍgaṃ śatacandraṃ ca bhānumat kṣurapreṇa śiraḥ kāyāt pātayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Śrutarvan, his chariot lost, O king, took up sword and shield; but even as he seized the sword and the gleaming shield bright with a hundred moons, the Pāṇḍava with a razor-edged shaft struck his head from his body.

sanskrit: chinnottamāṅgasya tataḥ kṣurapreṇa mahātmanaḥ papāta kāyaḥ sa rathād vasudhām anunādayan
english: Then, his head severed by the razor-shaft, the body of that great-souled warrior fell from the chariot, making the earth resound.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite vīre tāvakā bhayamohitāḥ abhyadravanta saṃgrāme bhīmasenaṃ yuyutsavaḥ
english: When that hero had fallen, your warriors, bewildered with fear yet eager to fight, rushed upon Bhīmasena in the battle.

sanskrit: tān āpatata evāśu hataśeṣād balārṇavāt daṃśitaḥ pratijagrāha bhīmasenaḥ pratāpavān te tu taṃ vai samāsādya parivavruḥ samantataḥ
english: As they swiftly charged from that ocean of host left over from the slain, the mailed and valiant Bhīmasena received them; and they, closing upon him, encircled him on every side.

sanskrit: tatas tu saṃvṛto bhīmas tāvakair niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ pīḍayām āsa tān sarvān sahasrākṣa ivāsurān
english: Then Bhīma, hemmed in by your men with their whetted arrows, harried them all as the thousand-eyed one harried the Asuras.

sanskrit: tataḥ pañcaśatān hatvā savarūthān mahārathān jaghāna kuñjarānīkaṃ punaḥ saptaśataṃ yudhi
english: Then, having slain five hundred great chariot-warriors with their car-guards, he struck down in the fight a host of elephants, seven hundred more.

sanskrit: hatvā daśa sahasrāṇi pattīnāṃ parameṣubhiḥ vājināṃ ca śatāny aṣṭau pāṇḍavaḥ sma virājate
english: Having slain ten thousand foot-soldiers with his supreme shafts, and eight hundred horse, the Pāṇḍava shone resplendent.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu kaunteyo hatvā yuddhe sutāṃs tava mene kṛtārtham ātmānaṃ saphalaṃ janma ca prabho
english: And Bhīmasena, son of Kuntī, having slain your sons in battle, deemed his purpose fulfilled and his birth made fruitful, O lord.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā yudhyamānaṃ ca vinighnantaṃ ca tāvakān īkṣituṃ notsahante sma tava sainyāni bhārata
english: As he thus fought on, cutting down your men, your troops could not bear even to look upon him, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vidrāvya tu kurūn sarvāṃs tāṃś ca hatvā padānugān dorbhyāṃ śabdaṃ tataś cakre trāsayāno mahādvipān
english: Having routed all the Kurus and slain their foot-followers, he made a din with his two arms, terrifying the great elephants.

sanskrit: hatabhūyiṣṭhayodhā tu tava senā viśāṃ pate kiṃciccheṣā mahārāja kṛpaṇā samapadyata
english: With the greater part of its warriors slain, your army, O lord of peoples, was reduced to a wretched remnant, O great king.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca duryodhano mahārāja sudarśaś cāpi te sutaḥ hataśeṣau tadā saṃkhye vājimadhye vyavasthitau
english: Saṃjaya said: Duryodhana, O great king, and Sudarśana too, your son, the survivors then of the slaughter, stood firm amid their horsemen on the field.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaṃ dṛṣṭvā vājimadhye vyavasthitam uvāca devakīputraḥ kuntīputraṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: Then, beholding Duryodhana posted among his horse, the son of Devakī spoke to Dhanaṃjaya, the son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: śatravo hatabhūyiṣṭhā jñātayaḥ paripālitāḥ gṛhītvā saṃjayaṃ cāsau nivṛttaḥ śinipuṃgavaḥ
english: "The foes are slain for the most part, our kinsmen are kept safe; and yonder bull of Śini's line has turned back, having taken Saṃjaya captive."

sanskrit: pariśrāntaś ca nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca bhārata yodhayitvā raṇe pāpān dhārtarāṣṭrapadānugān
english: "And Nakula is worn out, and Sahadeva too, O Bhārata, having fought in battle against the wicked retainers of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son."

sanskrit: suyodhanam abhityajya traya ete vyavasthitāḥ kṛpaś ca kṛtavarmā ca drauṇiś caiva mahārathaḥ
english: "Forsaking Suyodhana, these three stand apart: Kṛpa, and Kṛtavarman, and Droṇa's son, the great chariot-warrior."

sanskrit: asau tiṣṭhati pāñcālyaḥ śriyā paramayā yutaḥ duryodhanabalaṃ hatvā saha sarvaiḥ prabhadrakaiḥ
english: "Yonder stands the prince of Pāñcāla, endowed with surpassing splendor, having slain Duryodhana's host together with all the Prabhadrakas."

sanskrit: asau duryodhanaḥ pārtha vājimadhye vyavasthitaḥ chatreṇa dhriyamāṇena prekṣamāṇo muhur muhuḥ
english: "Yonder is Duryodhana, O Pārtha, posted amid his horsemen, the parasol held above him, gazing about again and again."

sanskrit: prativyūhya balaṃ sarvaṃ raṇamadhye vyavasthitaḥ enaṃ hatvā śitair bāṇaiḥ kṛtakṛtyo bhaviṣyasi
english: "Having marshalled his whole force, he stands in the midst of the field; slay him with your whetted arrows, and you shall have accomplished your end."

sanskrit: gajānīkaṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ ca prāptam ariṃdama yāvan na vidravanty ete tāvaj jahi suyodhanam
english: "Seeing the elephant-host destroyed and you come upon them, O subduer of foes, slay Suyodhana before these others scatter in flight."

sanskrit: yātu kaś cit tu pāñcālyaṃ kṣipram āgamyatām iti pariśrāntabalas tāta naiṣa mucyeta kilbiṣī
english: "Let someone go to the prince of Pāñcāla, bidding him come at once; for with his force worn out, this sinful one shall not escape, my friend."

sanskrit: tava hatvā balaṃ sarvaṃ saṃgrāme dhṛtarāṣṭrajaḥ jitān pāṇḍusutān matvā rūpaṃ dhārayate mahat
english: "Having slain your whole force in the battle, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, deeming the sons of Pāṇḍu vanquished, bears himself with a great show of pride."

sanskrit: nihataṃ svabalaṃ dṛṣṭvā pīḍitaṃ cāpi pāṇḍavaiḥ dhruvam eṣyati saṃgrāme vadhāyaivātmano nṛpaḥ
english: "Seeing his own host slain and hard-pressed by the Pāṇḍavas, the king will surely come into the battle, even unto his own destruction."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ phalgunas tu kṛṣṇaṃ vacanam abravīt dhṛtarāṣṭrasutāḥ sarve hatā bhīmena mānada yāv etāv āsthitau kṛṣṇa tāv adya na bhaviṣyataḥ
english: Thus addressed, Phalguna spoke this word to Kṛṣṇa: "All the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra have been slain by Bhīma, O giver of honor; and these two who yet stand, O Kṛṣṇa, this day shall be no more."

sanskrit: hato bhīṣmo hato droṇaḥ karṇo vaikartano hataḥ madrarājo hataḥ śalyo hataḥ kṛṣṇa jayadrathaḥ
english: "Bhīṣma is slain, Droṇa is slain, Karṇa son of Vikartana is slain; the king of the Madras is slain, Śalya is slain, and Jayadratha is slain, O Kṛṣṇa."

sanskrit: hayāḥ pañcaśatāḥ śiṣṭāḥ śakuneḥ saubalasya ca rathānāṃ tu śate śiṣṭe dve eva tu janārdana dantināṃ ca śataṃ sāgraṃ trisāhasrāḥ padātayaḥ
english: "Five hundred horse remain to Śakuni, son of Subala; and of chariots but two hundred remain, O Janārdana, and a full hundred of tusked elephants, and three thousand foot-soldiers."

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā kṛpaś caiva trigartādhipatis tathā ulūkaḥ śakuniś caiva kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ
english: "Aśvatthāman and Kṛpa, and the lord of the Trigartas likewise, Ulūka and Śakuni, and Kṛtavarman of the Sātvatas—"

sanskrit: etad balam abhūc cheṣaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya mādhava mokṣo na nūnaṃ kālād dhi vidyate bhuvi kasya cit
english: "—this is the force left to Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, O Mādhava; for surely from Time there is no deliverance upon the earth for any one."

sanskrit: tathā vinihate sainye paśya duryodhanaṃ sthitam adyāhnā hi mahārājo hatāmitro bhaviṣyati
english: "His army thus destroyed, behold Duryodhana standing firm; this very day shall the great king be left without a friend."

sanskrit: na hi me mokṣyate kaś cit pareṣām iti cintaye ye tv adya samaraṃ kṛṣṇa na hāsyanti raṇotkaṭāḥ tān vai sarvān haniṣyāmi yady api syur amānuṣāḥ
english: "For none of the foe shall escape me, so I resolve; and those fierce in battle, O Kṛṣṇa, who this day shall not abandon the fight—all of them I shall slay, even were they more than human."

sanskrit: adya yuddhe susaṃkruddho dīrghaṃ rājñaḥ prajāgaram apaneṣyāmi gāndhāraṃ pātayitvā śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: "This day in battle, sore enraged, I shall take away the long sleeplessness of the king, by felling the Gāndhāra prince with my whetted arrows."

sanskrit: nikṛtyā vai durācāro yāni ratnāni saubalaḥ sabhāyām aharad dyūte punas tāny āharāmy aham
english: "Those jewels which the evil-doing son of Subala, by his cheating, won from us at the dicing in the assembly hall—those I shall this day win back."

sanskrit: adya tā api vetsyanti sarvā nāgapurastriyaḥ śrutvā patīṃś ca putrāṃś ca pāṇḍavair nihatān yudhi
english: "This day too shall all the women of the City of the Elephant learn, hearing that their husbands and their sons have been slain by the Pāṇḍavas in the fight."

sanskrit: samāptam adya vai karma sarvaṃ kṛṣṇa bhaviṣyati adya duryodhano dīptāṃ śriyaṃ prāṇāṃś ca tyakṣyati
english: "This day shall all the work be brought to its end, O Kṛṣṇa; this day shall Duryodhana give up his blazing fortune and his life together."

sanskrit: nāpayāti bhayāt kṛṣṇa saṃgrāmād yadi cen mama nihataṃ viddhi vārṣṇeya dhārtarāṣṭraṃ subāliśam
english: "If, O Kṛṣṇa, he does not flee from the battle in fear of me, then know the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, that great fool, as already slain, O Vārṣṇeya."

sanskrit: mama hy etad aśaktaṃ vai vājivṛndam ariṃdama soḍhuṃ jyātalanirghoṣaṃ yāhi yāvan nihanmy aham
english: "For this throng of horses cannot bear the twang of my bowstring and the slap of my palm-guard, O subduer of foes; drive on, that I may slay them."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu dāśārhaḥ pāṇḍavena yaśasvinā acodayad dhayān rājan duryodhanabalaṃ prati
english: Thus addressed by the illustrious Pāṇḍava, the Dāśārha urged on the horses, O king, toward Duryodhana's host.

sanskrit: tad anīkam abhiprekṣya trayaḥ sajjā mahārathāḥ bhīmaseno 'rjunaś caiva sahadevaś ca māriṣa prayayuḥ siṃhanādena duryodhanajighāṃsayā
english: Beholding that array, three great chariot-warriors ready for battle—Bhīmasena and Arjuna and Sahadeva, O lord—advanced with a lion's roar, eager to slay Duryodhana.

sanskrit: tān prekṣya sahitān sarvāñ javenodyatakārmukān saubalo 'bhyadravad yuddhe pāṇḍavān ātatāyinaḥ
english: Seeing them all together, sweeping on at speed with bows uplifted, the son of Subala charged in battle against the Pāṇḍavas, those bringers of doom.

sanskrit: sudarśanas tava suto bhīmasenaṃ samabhyayāt suśarmā śakuniś caiva yuyudhāte kirīṭinā sahadevaṃ tava suto hayapṛṣṭhagato 'bhyayāt
english: Sudarśana, your son, advanced against Bhīmasena; Suśarman and Śakuni did battle with the Diademed One; and your son, mounted upon a horse's back, advanced against Sahadeva.

sanskrit: tato hy ayatnataḥ kṣipraṃ tava putro janādhipa prāsena sahadevasya śirasi prāharad bhṛśam
english: Then swiftly and without effort, your son, O lord of men, smote Sahadeva hard upon the head with a javelin.

sanskrit: sopāviśad rathopasthe tava putreṇa tāḍitaḥ rudhirāplutasarvāṅga āśīviṣa iva śvasan
english: Struck down by your son, he sank upon the floor of his chariot, all his limbs bathed in blood, hissing like a venomous serpent.

sanskrit: pratilabhya tataḥ saṃjñāṃ sahadevo viśāṃ pate duryodhanaṃ śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ saṃkruddhaḥ samavākirat
english: Then, regaining his senses, Sahadeva, O lord of peoples, in his wrath covered Duryodhana with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: pārtho 'pi yudhi vikramya kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ śūrāṇām aśvapṛṣṭhebhyaḥ śirāṃsi nicakarta ha
english: Pārtha too, displaying his prowess in the fight—Dhanaṃjaya, son of Kuntī—struck the heads of the brave warriors from off their horses' backs.

sanskrit: tad anīkaṃ tadā pārtho vyadhamad bahubhiḥ śaraiḥ pātayitvā hayān sarvāṃs trigartānāṃ rathān yayau
english: Then Pārtha scattered that array with his many arrows, and felling all the horses, drove against the chariots of the Trigartas.

sanskrit: tatas te sahitā bhūtvā trigartānāṃ mahārathāḥ arjunaṃ vāsudevaṃ ca śaravarṣair avākiran
english: Then the great chariot-warriors of the Trigartas, joining together, overwhelmed Arjuna and Vāsudeva with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: satyakarmāṇam ākṣipya kṣurapreṇa mahāyaśāḥ tato 'sya syandanasyeṣāṃ cicchide pāṇḍunandanaḥ
english: Assailing Satyakarman, the greatly renowned son of Pāṇḍu cut apart with a razor-shaft the pole of his chariot.

sanskrit: śilāśitena ca vibho kṣurapreṇa mahāyaśāḥ śiraś ciccheda prahasaṃs taptakuṇḍalabhūṣaṇam
english: And with a razor-shaft honed upon stone, O lord, that greatly renowned one, smiling, severed his head, adorned with burnished earrings.

sanskrit: satyeṣum atha cādatta yodhānāṃ miṣatāṃ tataḥ yathā siṃho vane rājan mṛgaṃ paribubhukṣitaḥ
english: Then, before the very eyes of the warriors, he seized upon Satyeṣu, as a lion in the forest, O king, seizes a deer in its hunger.

sanskrit: taṃ nihatya tataḥ pārthaḥ suśarmāṇaṃ tribhiḥ śaraiḥ viddhvā tān ahanat sarvān rathān rukmavibhūṣitān
english: Having slain him, Pārtha then pierced Suśarman with three arrows, and struck down all those chariots adorned with gold.

sanskrit: tatas tu pratvaran pārtho dīrghakālaṃ susaṃbhṛtam muñcan krodhaviṣaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ prasthalādhipatiṃ prati
english: Then, pressing swiftly on, Pārtha loosed the keen venom of a wrath long gathered up against the lord of Prasthala.

sanskrit: tam arjunaḥ pṛṣatkānāṃ śatena bharatarṣabha pūrayitvā tato vāhān nyahanat tasya dhanvinaḥ
english: Arjuna, O bull of the Bharatas, having filled him with a hundred shafts, then slew the horses of that bowman.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaraṃ samādāya yamadaṇḍopamaṃ śitam suśarmāṇaṃ samuddiśya cikṣepāśu hasann iva
english: Then, taking up a whetted arrow like the rod of Yama, he aimed at Suśarman and loosed it swiftly, as though in mirth.

sanskrit: sa śaraḥ preṣitas tena krodhadīptena dhanvinā suśarmāṇaṃ samāsādya bibheda hṛdayaṃ raṇe
english: That arrow, sped by that bowman blazing with wrath, reached Suśarman and clove his heart in the battle.

sanskrit: sa gatāsur mahārāja papāta dharaṇītale nandayan pāṇḍavān sarvān vyathayaṃś cāpi tāvakān
english: Lifeless, O great king, he fell upon the surface of the earth, gladdening all the Pāṇḍavas and grieving your men.

sanskrit: suśarmāṇaṃ raṇe hatvā putrān asya mahārathān sapta cāṣṭau ca triṃśac ca sāyakair anayat kṣayam
english: Having slain Suśarman in battle, he brought to destruction with his shafts the sons of that warrior, great chariot-fighters, five and forty in number.

sanskrit: tato 'sya niśitair bāṇaiḥ sarvān hatvā padānugān abhyagād bhāratīṃ senāṃ hataśeṣāṃ mahārathaḥ
english: Then, having slain all his foot-followers with his whetted arrows, that great chariot-warrior advanced upon the remnant of the Bhārata host.

sanskrit: bhīmas tu samare kruddhaḥ putraṃ tava janādhipa sudarśanam adṛśyaṃ taṃ śaraiś cakre hasann iva
english: But Bhīma, wrathful in the battle, made your son Sudarśana invisible with his arrows, O lord of men, as though smiling the while.

sanskrit: tato 'sya prahasan kruddhaḥ śiraḥ kāyād apāharat kṣurapreṇa sutīkṣṇena sa hataḥ prāpatad bhuvi
english: Then, smiling in his wrath, he struck his head from his body with a keen razor-shaft; slain, he fell to the earth.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu nihate vīre tatas tasya padānugāḥ parivavrū raṇe bhīmaṃ kiranto viśikhāñ śitān
english: When that hero had been slain, his foot-followers then encircled Bhīma in the battle, scattering their whetted shafts.

sanskrit: tatas tu niśitair bāṇais tad anīkaṃ vṛkodaraḥ indrāśanisamasparśaiḥ samantāt paryavākirat tataḥ kṣaṇena tad bhīmo nyahanad bharatarṣabha
english: Then Vṛkodara with his whetted arrows, whose touch was like the thunderbolt of Indra, covered that array on every side; and in a moment, O bull of the Bharatas, Bhīma cut it down.

sanskrit: teṣu tūtsādyamāneṣu senādhyakṣā mahābalāḥ bhīmasenaṃ samāsādya tato 'yudhyanta bhārata tāṃs tu sarvāñ śarair ghorair avākirata pāṇḍavaḥ
english: As these were being destroyed, the mighty captains of the host closed with Bhīmasena and gave battle, O Bhārata; and the Pāṇḍava covered them all with his terrible arrows.

sanskrit: tathaiva tāvakā rājan pāṇḍaveyān mahārathān śaravarṣeṇa mahatā samantāt paryavārayan
english: In like manner your men, O king, hemmed in on every side the great chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas with a mighty rain of arrows.

sanskrit: vyākulaṃ tad abhūt sarvaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ paraiḥ saha tāvakānāṃ ca samare pāṇḍaveyair yuyutsatām
english: All was thrown into confusion—the Pāṇḍavas locked with the foe, and your men in the battle striving against the followers of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: tatra yodhās tadā petuḥ parasparasamāhatāḥ ubhayoḥ senayo rājan saṃśocantaḥ sma bāndhavān
english: There the warriors then fell, smiting one another down, in both the armies, O king, grieving for their kinsmen.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasmin pravṛtte saṃgrāme naravājigajakṣaye śakuniḥ saubalo rājan sahadevaṃ samabhyayāt
english: Saṃjaya said: As that battle, the destroyer of men and horses and elephants, raged on, Śakuni, son of Subala, O king, advanced against Sahadeva.

sanskrit: tato 'syāpatatas tūrṇaṃ sahadevaḥ pratāpavān śaraughān preṣayām āsa pataṃgān iva śīghragān ulūkaś ca raṇe bhīmaṃ vivyādha daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then, as he charged swiftly on, the valiant Sahadeva sent forth floods of arrows, swift-flying like locusts; and Ulūka in the battle pierced Bhīma with ten shafts.

sanskrit: śakunis tu mahārāja bhīmaṃ viddhvā tribhiḥ śaraiḥ sāyakānāṃ navatyā vai sahadevam avākirat
english: And Śakuni, O great king, having pierced Bhīma with three arrows, then covered Sahadeva with ninety shafts.

sanskrit: te śūrāḥ samare rājan samāsādya parasparam vivyadhur niśitair bāṇaiḥ kaṅkabarhiṇavājitaiḥ svarṇapuṅkhaiḥ śilādhautair ā karṇāt prahitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Those heroes, O king, closing with one another in the battle, pierced each other with whetted arrows fledged with heron and peacock feathers, golden-nocked, honed upon stone, and drawn back to the ear before they were loosed.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ cāpabhujotsṛṣṭā śaravṛṣṭir viśāṃ pate ācchādayad diśaḥ sarvā dhārābhir iva toyadaḥ
english: The shower of arrows loosed from their bow-arms, O lord of peoples, veiled all the quarters, as a rain-cloud veils them with its torrents.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho raṇe bhīmaḥ sahadevaś ca bhārata ceratuḥ kadanaṃ saṃkhye kurvantau sumahābalau
english: Then Bhīma, wrathful in the battle, and Sahadeva, O Bhārata, those two of exceeding might, ranged the field, working havoc in the fray.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ śaraśataiś channaṃ tad balaṃ tava bhārata andhakāram ivākāśam abhavat tatra tatra ha
english: Shrouded by their hundreds of arrows, that host of yours, O Bhārata, became here and there as dark as a sky filled with gloom.
